mainTopic: Whether hidden impurity (טומאה טמונה) breaks through according to רבי יוסי, the contradiction from the dead dog on the threshold and רבא's answer, and who argues with רבי יוסי
overview: The גמרא cites a ברייתא where רבי יוסי declares something טהור, and asks which case of the משנה he is arguing about. He must be arguing on the case of impurity inside a chest in the house. There he rejects both of the תנא קמא's reasons, which shows he holds טומאה טמונה אינה בוקעת: hidden impurity does not break through. The גמרא then raises a contradiction from the משנה about a dead dog that ate flesh of a corpse and lies on a doorstep. There רבי יוסי seems to make the house טמא even when the impurity is hidden inside the dog. רבא answers that רבי יוסי looks at the empty space around the impurity, and that he disagrees with רבי מאיר on two points: the neck's טפח must be real open space, and only impurity from the lintel inward makes the house טמא. רב אחא בריה דרבא has a version of the משנה that says this outright. Finally the גמרא asks which תנא argues with רבי יוסי on whether touching and overlying combine, and answers that it is רבי שמעון, starting a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי יוסי rules it pure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that רבי יוסי declares the case טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches about this משנה: רבי יוסי says it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds רבי יוסי's opinion to the משנה. It does not yet say which case he is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells us רבי יוסי disagrees and rules טהור. It does not say which clause of the משנה he is arguing on. That missing detail sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: And a ברייתא teaches about it (adds to the משנה)
Declares it pure (טהור)

phrases.english: And it is taught about it:
phrases.notes: "It" is the משנה the גמרא was just discussing, about impurity and a chest in a house.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei declares it pure.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי rules טהור in some case of the משנה.

steps.title: Which case is רבי יוסי talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which clause of the משנה רבי יוסי is arguing on.
steps.simpleTranslation: On which case is he arguing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which part of the משנה רבי יוסי's ruling of טהור goes on. This question sets up the next moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot understand רבי יוסי's opinion until we know which case he means. Once we know, we can work out his reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: On which one? (which case does this refer to)

phrases.english: To which [case does this refer]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks where the ברייתא's ruling belongs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which clause of the משנה רבי יוסי is arguing on.

steps.title: It can't be the later clause
steps.stepSummary: It cannot be the later clause, because the תנא קמא already rules טהור there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he is arguing on the later clause, that doesn't work. The תנא קמא also says טהור there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the later clause of the משנה and rejects it. There is no argument there, because the תנא קמא also says טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא would only mention רבי יוסי if he disagrees with someone. In the later clause everyone already says טהור, so there is nothing for him to disagree with.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offers a suggestion that will be rejected)
The later clause of a משנה
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: If you say [it refers] to the latter clause –
phrases.notes: The later part of the משנה, which deals with the chest placed at the entrance.

phrases.english: the first tanna also
declares it pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one possible answer to the question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבי יוסי is arguing on the later clause.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תנא קמא already says טהור there, so there would be no argument.

steps.title: It's the case of impurity inside the chest
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי argues on the case where the תנא קמא says the house is טמא, for one of two possible reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he is arguing on the case where the תנא קמא says: if the impurity is inside the chest, the house is טמא. That is either because impurity will eventually come out, or because hidden impurity breaks through.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי is arguing on the earlier case, where the תנא קמא makes the house טמא. It gives two possible reasons for the תנא קמא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one: the impure item will eventually be taken out of the chest through the house (דרך טומאה לצאת). Reason two: impurity that is closed in still pushes up and out (טומאה טמונה בוקעת). The next step shows רבי יוסי rejecting both.

keyTerms.meaning: The impurity will eventually be taken out, so the house counts as its path
Hidden, closed-in impurity
Breaks through (and spreads upward)

phrases.english: Rather, [it refers to] where the first tanna says:
impurity inside it – the house is impure,
phrases.notes: "It" means the compartment of the chest sitting inside the house.

phrases.english: either because the way of impurity is to go out,
or because hidden impurity breaks through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct answer after the first suggestion was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי argues on the case where the תנא קמא says the house is טמא because of impurity inside the chest.

steps.title: רבי יוסי rejects both reasons
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers both reasons. This shows he holds that hidden impurity does not break through.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says to him: You said the impurity will come out? It can be taken out in pieces or burned where it is. You said hidden impurity breaks through? Hidden impurity does not break through.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers each of the תנא קמא's two reasons, one at a time. In doing so, he states that טומאה טמונה אינה בוקעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Against reason one: the item does not have to come out whole through the house. It can be taken out in small pieces or burned inside the chest. Against reason two: he simply denies it and says hidden impurity does not break through. This statement becomes the basis for the contradiction that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: In halves or pieces
To burn it where it is
Does not break through

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי holds טומאה טמונה אינה בוקעת: hidden impurity does not break through.
steps.whyThisMatters: This clear position is what the גמרא will now compare against another ruling of רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei says to him:
And as for what you said, that the way of impurity is to go out –
he can take it out in halves
phrases.notes: He means it doesn't have to pass through the house in one piece, so the whole house isn't its path.

phrases.english: or burn it in its place,
and as for what you said, that hidden impurity breaks through –
hidden impurity does not break through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי יוסי's reply to the two reasons just given.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impurity can be removed in pieces or burned in place, and טומאה טמונה אינה בוקעת.

steps.title: A contradiction between two rulings of רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets one statement of רבי יוסי against another of his statements.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא points out a contradiction between this ruling of רבי יוסי and another ruling of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that רבי יוסי seems to contradict himself. The source for this comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that רבי יוסי holds hidden impurity does not break through. The גמרא is about to show another case where he seems to hold that it does.

keyTerms.meaning: And he points out a contradiction (sets two sources against each other)

phrases.english: And he raises a contradiction between Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the position just established for רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's view that טומאה טמונה אינה בוקעת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ruling of his seems to assume hidden impurity does break through, so his two rulings would clash.

steps.title: The משנה of the dog on the threshold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the משנה about a dead dog that ate flesh of a corpse, starting with רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: a dog ate flesh of a dead person, then the dog died and is lying on the doorway. רבי מאיר says: if its neck is a טפח wide, it brings the impurity into the house; if not, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the source for the contradiction. The גמרא is setting it up: here it quotes רבי מאיר, and רבי יוסי's opinion, which creates the clash, comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The impure flesh is hidden inside the dog's body. רבי מאיר counts the width of the neck, including its walls, even when its hollow is less than a טפח: the neck's width acts like an אוהל that channels the impurity into the house. Watch how רבי יוסי rules on this hidden impurity in the next part.

keyTerms.meaning: Flesh of a dead person
Threshold of a doorway
An open space of one handbreadth
Brings the impurity in (spreads it into the house)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not yet the contradiction itself. רבי מאיר speaks first; רבי יוסי's opinion, which creates the clash, comes after this.

phrases.english: As we learned: A dog that ate flesh of a corpse,
and the dog died, and is lying on the threshold –
Rabbi Meir says:
If there is in its neck an opening of a handbreadth –
it brings in the impurity,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו – אֵינוֹ מֵבִיא אֶת הַטּוּמְאָה.
phrases.english: and if not – it does not bring in the impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts quoting the source for the contradiction announced in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the dead dog brings impurity into the house if its neck is a טפח wide, even if its hollow is smaller.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: It depends on where the dog lies relative to the lintel
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues with רבי יוסי's view: if the dog lies under the lintel or further inside, the house is טמא. If it lies further outside, the house is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: We look at where the dog is. If it is from under the lintel and inward, the house is impure. If it is from under the lintel and outward, the house is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה about the dead dog, now giving רבי יוסי's opinion. This is the line the גמרא will analyze in Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a plain reading, רבי יוסי's words speak about where the dog is lying, not about how wide its neck is. If the טומאה inside the dog is under the lintel or inside the house, the house becomes טמא. Steps 10–13 look more closely at which case he really means.

keyTerms.meaning: The lintel, the beam across the top of a doorway
'We look,' meaning we check the exact position
Inward, toward the inside of the house
Outward, toward the outside

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. רבי מאיר looked at the dog's neck. At first glance רבי יוסי looks only at where the dog is lying compared to the lintel, but רבא shows in steps 12–13 that he also argues about the open space in the neck.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: One looks
phrases.notes: He means we check exactly where on the doorstep the dog is lying.

phrases.english: from opposite the lintel and inward, the house is impure;
phrases.notes: 'Opposite the lintel' means directly under it.

phrases.english: from opposite the lintel and outward, the house is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the משנה that Step 7 began with רבי מאיר's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, the house is טמא if the dog lies from under the lintel inward, and טהור if it lies from under the lintel outward.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר and רבי יהודה בן בתירא: It depends on which way the dog faces
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that if the dog's mouth faces in, the house is טהור, and if its mouth faces out, the house is טמא, because the טומאה exits from the rear. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says the house is טמא either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: If its mouth is inside, the house is pure. If its mouth is outside, the house is impure, because the impurity leaves through its rear. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: Either way, the house is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה with two more opinions about the dog on the doorstep. They are quoted to complete the picture, but the גמרא's question in the next step is about רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that the טומאה comes out of the dog through its rear end. So the house is טמא only if the rear faces inside. רבי יהודה בן בתירא holds that the טומאה can come out through either end, so the house is טמא no matter which way the dog lies.

keyTerms.meaning: Its mouth
Its edge, meaning the dog's rear end
Goes out, exits
Either way, in both cases

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: פִּיו לִפְנִים הַבַּיִת – טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says: If its mouth is inside, the house is pure;
if its mouth is outside, the house is impure,
phrases.notes: If the mouth faces out, the rear end is inside the house.

phrases.english: because the impurity exits through its rear.
Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ, הַבַּיִת טָמֵא.
phrases.english: Either way, the house is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: פִּיו לִפְנִים הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the משנה begun in Steps 7 and 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: the house is טמא only if the dog's rear is inside. רבי יהודה בן בתירא: the house is טמא in either direction.

steps.title: Is רבי יוסי talking about a dog whose neck has no opening of a טפח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוסי is answering רבי מאיר's case, where the neck has no opening of a טפח. If so, רבי יוסי holds the house is טמא even though the טומאה is hidden inside the dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not so that רבי יוסי is talking about the case where there is no opening of a טפח in the dog's neck?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the משנה it just quoted to build its contradiction against רבי יוסי. It suggests which case רבי יוסי is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said that if the dog's neck has no opening of a טפח, the house stays טהור. If רבי יוסי is arguing on that very case and still calls the house טמא, then he holds that hidden טומאה does break through. That clashes with Step 5, where he held hidden טומאה does not break through.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What, is it not...?' The גמרא is suggesting how to read a source
Its neck
Stands on, meaning is referring to

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the second half of the contradiction set up in Step 6. Read this way, the משנה shows רבי יוסי holding the opposite of his position in Step 5.

phrases.english: What, is it not
regarding the case where there is no opening of a handbreadth in its neck
that Rabbi Yosei is referring?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו, אַאֵין בְּצַוָּארוֹ פּוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח קָאֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה quoted in Steps 7 to 9 to show the second side of the contradiction announced in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's view in Step 5 that hidden טומאה does not break through.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יוסי rules the house טמא even when the dog's neck has no opening of a טפח, then the hidden טומאה inside the dog is affecting the house. That means hidden טומאה does break through, which contradicts his other statement.

steps.title: So hidden impurity breaks through?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the troubling conclusion: according to this reading, רבי יוסי holds that טומאה טמונה בוקעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it: hidden impurity breaks through!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it began in the last step. If רבי יוסי makes the house טמא, he must hold that hidden impurity spreads out, and that contradicts his other statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 the גמרא assumed רבי יוסי is talking about רבי מאיר's case, where the dog's neck has no opening of a טפח. In that case the flesh inside the dog is fully hidden. If the house is still טמא, then hidden impurity must break out of its covering, and that clashes with רבי יוסי's statement in step 5 that טומאה טמונה אינה בוקעת.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: we can draw this conclusion

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion of רבי יוסי. The גמרא is saying 'if we read him this way, look where it leads', and that result is the problem.

phrases.english: And learn from it: hidden impurity breaks through!
phrases.notes: This clashes with רבי יוסי's statement in step 5 that hidden impurity does not break through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the inference started in step 10 and turns it into a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling in the משנה about the dead dog
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the house is טמא even though the neck has no opening, the hidden flesh must break through. That contradicts רבי יוסי's other statement.

steps.title: רבא: look at the empty space, and the first disagreement
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי יוסי's words mean 'we look at the empty space of the impurity'. He also says רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי מאיר on two points. The first is that the טפח opening must be real empty space.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It teaches 'one looks at the empty space of the impurity.' רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי מאיר on two matters, and says to him: As for what you said, that if there is an opening of a טפח in its neck it brings the impurity in, we go after its empty space.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction. He reads רבי יוסי as talking about the empty space around the impurity, not about impurity that is completely hidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said a neck with a טפח opening brings the impurity into the house. רבי יוסי answers that we measure only the empty space: the טפח must be open air, not counting the thickness of the neck's flesh. If there is a real open space, the impurity is not simply 'hidden', so רבי יוסי does not need to hold that טומאה טמונה בוקעת.

keyTerms.meaning: The empty space of the impurity: the open air space next to the impure item
He disagrees on two points
We go after its empty space: only real open space counts

steps.whyThisMatters: This reading removes the contradiction. רבי יוסי can keep his view that hidden impurity does not break out.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: רוֹאִין אֶת חֲלַל הַטּוּמְאָה קָתָנֵי,
phrases.english: Rava said: It teaches 'one looks at the empty space of the impurity,'
and Rabbi Yosei disagrees on two matters,
and he says to Rabbi Meir:

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָאָמְרַתְּ כִּי יֵשׁ בְּצַוָּארוֹ פּוֹתֵחַ טֶפַח
phrases.english: That which you said, that when there is an opening of a handbreadth in its neck
it brings the impurity in –
we go after its empty space.
phrases.notes: He means the full טפח has to be open space. The flesh of the neck does not count toward it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: רוֹאִין אֶת חֲלַל הַטּוּמְאָה קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 10–11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה: רבי יוסי speaks about empty space, not about fully hidden impurity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי makes the house טמא even when the impurity is completely hidden inside the dog.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי requires a real טפח of empty space. So the impurity is not treated as hidden, and there is no contradiction.

steps.title: The second disagreement: where the dog lies
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues. רבי יוסי also disagrees with רבי מאיר that the whole house is always טמא. It depends on whether the impurity is inside or outside the line of the שקוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for what you said, that the whole house is טמא: from opposite the lintel and inward, the house is טמא; from opposite the lintel and outward, the house is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the second point where רבי יוסי argues with רבי מאיר. This one is about where the dog is lying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר made the whole house טמא even if the dog lay on the outer part of the threshold. רבי יוסי draws a line at the שקוף. If the impurity is from that line inward, the house is טמא. If it is from that line outward, the house stays טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Lintel: the beam across the top of a doorway
From opposite (the line) and inward
And outward

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, רבי יוסי argues with רבי מאיר on two points: (1) the טפח must be real empty space; (2) only impurity from the line of the שקוף and inward makes the house טמא.

phrases.english: And that which you said, that the entire house is impure –
from opposite the lintel and inward, the house is impure,
from opposite the lintel and outward, the house is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second of the two disagreements רבא announced in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Completing the reading of רבי יוסי's two disagreements
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי's lintel ruling is about location only. It does not say that hidden impurity breaks through.

steps.title: רב אחא's version says it outright
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא says the משנה itself is worded this way: רבי יוסי says 'one looks at the empty space of the impurity.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא teaches it explicitly: רבי יוסי says, one looks at the empty space of the impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a version of the משנה that already has רבא's wording in it. So רבא's reading is not a guess; this version says it in plain words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had to explain רבי יוסי's words as meaning 'the empty space of the impurity.' רב אחא בריה דרבא learns the משנה with those exact words written in it. That backs up רבא's answer to the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Explicitly, in plain words

steps.whatToRemember: The contradiction in רבי יוסי is solved. He looks at the empty space of the impurity, so he never says that hidden impurity breaks through.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּהֶדְיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, teaches it explicitly:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: רוֹאִין אֶת חֲלַל הַטּוּמְאָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: One looks at the empty space of the impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּהֶדְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's reading by bringing a version of the משנה that says it outright.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the משנה, רבי יוסי's words are 'רואין את חלל הטומאה': we look at the empty space of the impurity.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's answer stands, and the two statements of רבי יוסי no longer clash.

steps.title: Who is the תנא who argues on רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא disagrees with רבי יוסי and holds that touching and overlying are separate kinds of טומאה that do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא who disagrees with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple identification question: which תנא holds the opposite of רבי יוסי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that מגע and אהל are one category, so two halves of a כזית can join together. The משנה in אהלות says the person stays טהור, so the halves do not join. The גמרא wants to know whose opinion that משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period whose view is recorded in a משנה or ברייתא
Who disagrees with him
Overlying, being over or under the same cover as the טומאה, which passes on impurity

phrases.english: And who is the tanna who disagrees with him?
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי יוסי. The question is who holds that touching and overlying do not join together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from explaining רבי יוסי's view to finding the תנא who argues with him on whether מגע and אהל combine.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds that מגע and אהל are separate categories, as the משנה in אהלות implies.

steps.title: It is רבי שמעון, as a ברייתא shows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the disagreeing תנא is רבי שמעון, and starts quoting a ברייתא with his opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי שמעון, as it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבי שמעון as the תנא who argues on רבי יוסי. It then sets up the proof by starting to quote a ברייתא. His actual words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer has two parts: a name (רבי שמעון) and a source (a ברייתא). The proof itself only appears once the ברייתא's content is quoted, so this line is a setup for the next move.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Shimon,
as it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the identification question from step 15 and begins bringing a ברייתא as support.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא who disagrees with רבי יוסי is רבי שמעון. A ברייתא with his view is about to be quoted.
